To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

KSHV-associated MCD and KSHV inflammatory cytokerine syndrome are two related but distinct entities, both characterized by systemic inflammation, elevated KSHV load and viral lytic activation, and both associated with a poor prognosis.
KSHV lytically activates B cells in patients with KSHMCD and KICS, and this leads to overproduction of inflammatory cytokines and systemic symptoms.

KSHV-associated multicentric Castleman Disease and KSHV Inflammatoyr Cytokine Syndromes are distinct clinical entities that share a number of features, including the production of viral and human cytokines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the clinical manifestations of KSHV lytically activated cells and the pathogenesis of the KSHV-associated disorders KICS and KSV-MCD.
the pathogenesis and clinical manifestations of KSHV-related disorders including MCD and KICS.
the clinical manifestations and pathogenesis of KSHV lytically reactivated states, including KSHV-MDC, KICS and KS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pathogenesis of KSHV-related MCD and KICS is incompletely understood.
KSHV is associated with a spectrum of clinical disorders including KICS, KSHV-MCDC, and KS.

KSHV-associated MCD and KSHV-associated KICS are distinct entities that are characterized by a common set of clinical, laboratory, and pathologic findings and that both of these disorders are associated with KSHV infection and overproduction of vIL- 6.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
KSHV lytically infected cells are the source of inflammatory cytokines that contribute to clinical disease.
KICS and KSVH-MCD are both associated with the production of KSHV vIL-6.
KSHV lytically activated B cell proliferation is associated with a spectrum of disease manifestations including KICS, KSHV-MC and perhaps other inflammatory conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lytic activation of KSHV can lead to the development of inflammatory disorders in patients infected with KSH.
the clinical spectrum of KS-associated herpesvirus lytic activation is much broader than was appreciated a few years ago.
the lytic cycle of KSHV can be a major contributor to disease in patients with KSHVS-associated diseases.
